story.title: Democrats Select South Carolina for First Presidential Primary in 2028
story.summary: The Democratic National Committee has recommended that South Carolina hold the first presidential primary for the 2028 election cycle. This decision marks a significant shift in the primary calendar, as South Carolina will replace Iowa as the opening contest. The move aims to prioritize representation among Black and Latino voters, with Nevada also scheduled for an early primary.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed in the 2028 calendar?
explore_lenses.title: A six-state early window, not a new Iowa switch
explore_lenses.summary: The Rules and Bylaws Committee proposed retaining South Carolina as the first Democratic contest, rather than newly moving it ahead of Iowa for 2028. It also expanded the early window to six states and set proposed dates through February.

claims.text: The committee proposed South Carolina for January 22, 2028, followed by Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan, and Virginia; Iowa is not among the six early-window states.

South Carolina had already been moved to the front of the Democratic calendar for the 2024 cycle, so the 2026 vote would preserve that lead position for 2028 rather than make the initial change from Iowa.
The committee amended its earlier process, which contemplated four or five early states, to permit a sixth state after reviewing applications.

explore_lenses.label: What did supporters and opponents argue?
explore_lenses.title: Representation, competitiveness, and state-law concerns
explore_lenses.summary: South Carolina advocates framed first position as recognition of Black voters, while Nevada advocates emphasized Latino voters and battleground-state experience. Leaders in Iowa and New Hampshire objected on different grounds, including New Hampshire's statutory scheduling requirement.

claims.text: Former DNC Chair Jaime Harrison said retaining South Carolina first would signal to Black voters that their role in the party is valued; South Carolina supporters also argued that the state offers an established test of candidates' support among Black voters.
Nevada DNC Vice Chair Artie Blanco argued Nevada should lead because it is a battleground state and because Latino voters play an increasingly important role in the party's future.

Iowa Democratic Party Chair Rita Hart called the process “very messy” and said the national party was out of touch with voters, while New Hampshire Democratic Party Chair Ray Buckley said the committee vote did not alter constraints on the state's primary.

explore_lenses.label: What must happen before the calendar takes effect?
explore_lenses.title: Full-DNC approval and possible compliance disputes
explore_lenses.summary: The full DNC is scheduled to vote on the proposal in August. Even if approved, implementation could face a conflict with New Hampshire's state-law timing requirement and any state decision to hold an unsanctioned contest.

claims.text: The full DNC is scheduled to consider the Rules and Bylaws Committee proposal at its August 13-15, 2026 summer meeting.

New Hampshire's secretary of state is required by state law to schedule its presidential primary at least seven days before a similar contest elsewhere, which conflicts with the proposed January 22 South Carolina date and February 8 New Hampshire date.

Under rule changes adopted by the committee in June, a state that holds an unsanctioned early contest could lose all delegates and automatic delegates and face a $270,000 fine; candidates who violate the rules could be barred from DNC debates and early-window delegates.

related_stories.title: Trump Issues Order for Warnings on 'Inaccurate' History at Smithsonian
related_stories.summary: President Donald Trump has issued an executive order requiring the installation of signage at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History. The signs will warn visitors about what the administration deems 'inaccurate historical information' within the museum. This move follows ongoing accusations from the Trump administration of anti-American bias in the museum's exhibits.

related_stories.title: Indian Education Minister Resigns Amid Youth Protests Over Exam Scandal
related_stories.summary: Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned as India's education minister following widespread protests by youth over exam paper leaks. The protests, led by a movement referred to as 'Cockroach,' culminated in celebrations among demonstrators after Pradhan's resignation was announced. The movement's leaders indicated that the government had accepted their demands, leading to the decision to end the protests.

related_stories.title: International Criminal Court Votes to Remove Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan
related_stories.summary: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has voted to remove Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan amid allegations of sexual misconduct. The decision comes nearly two years after the allegations first emerged. Khan has denied the accusations, which include claims of engaging in an improper relationship with a junior staff member and attempting to prevent her from pursuing her complaint.

related_stories.title: Maine Democrats Set to Nominate Troy Jackson for Senate Race
related_stories.summary: Maine Democrats are convening to select a Senate nominee to replace Graham Platner, with former state Senate President Troy Jackson expected to secure the nomination. Jackson, who comes from a logging family, is preparing to challenge Republican Senator Susan Collins in the upcoming election, which is being closely watched nationally. Collins has significantly outpaced Jackson in fundraising, raising over $16 million compared to Jackson's $1 million since entering the race.
